newsitem.title: USA: DPUC says no basis for Northeast credits.
newsitem.headline: DPUC says no basis for Northeast credits.

text.p: The Connecticut Department of Public Utility Control (DPUC) on Friday rejected a request by the state's attorney general to order a one-time, 25 percent credit for all customers of Northeast Utilities subsidiary Connecticut Light & Power.

Attorney General Richard Blumenthal on June 6 proposed credits on customers' July electric bills, worth a total $33 million, because he believed customers could not count on reliable electric service.

The DPUC said in a letter to Blumenthal that it must give due process to the issue of possible mismanagement at Northeast Utilities, whose three Millstone nuclear plants are all closed for safety reasons.
The DPUC said it would be premature to order rate reductions. A DPUC spokesperson was not immediately available for comment.
The department said it would not commence another hearing to examine Connecticut Light & Power's rates or nuclear operations.
Blumenthal said in a brief statement that he was disappointed by the DPUC's decision.
"This is a quality of service issue," he said. "Consumers are not getting what they are paying for."
Blumenthal said that as a basic matter of fairness, "CL&P's customers deserve the oppportunity to be heard on this issue and to receive appropriate relief."
Northeast has projected its total nuclear-related losses at $990 million, from April 1996 through 1998.
The utility has said that it intends to have all three of its Millstone plants in Waterford, Conn., ready to be restarted by early 1998, pending approval by federal regulators.
